cards.explanation: The answer is who the crowds say He is. Jesus asks, "Who do the crowds say I am?" (Luke 9:18). He starts with what everyone else is saying before He asks about the people right in front of Him. I think that's a smart way to ease into a big question.

The answer is True. The disciples say, "Some say John the Baptist…" (Luke 9:19). John was the man who preached baptism around the Jordan (Luke 3:3). So some people looked at Jesus and saw John. That's one theory out of several.

The answer is Christ. Peter answers, "The Christ of God." (Luke 9:20). The crowds were throwing out names like John the Baptist and Elijah (Luke 9:19). It's like a group chat full of guesses, and one person just texts the answer.

The answer is False, and it's a surprise. Luke 9:21 says, "Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone." That's the opposite of go tell everyone. The text doesn't give a reason, so we leave it right there.

The answer is the elders, chief priests and scribes. Jesus says the Son of Man "…must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes…" (Luke 9:22). Those are three groups, and He names all of them. I think that's a hard thing to hear, and Jesus says it straight.

The answer is that He will be raised to life. That's the good part. Jesus says He "…must be killed and on the third day be raised to life." (Luke 9:22). The hard news and the hopeful news come in the same sentence. Don't stop reading before the third day, friends.

The answer is a cross. Jesus says, "…he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me." (Luke 9:23). Notice the word daily. He doesn't say once, He says daily. No fine print, just plain words.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "For whoever wants to save his life will lose it…" (Luke 9:24). The one who wants to save his life is the one who loses it, not the one who keeps it. The other half of the verse shows the other side: "…but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it."

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it." (Luke 9:24). Notice the words "…for My sake…" The losing He's talking about is for Him. It's the flip side of the first half, where wanting to save your life ends in losing it.

The answer is his very self. Jesus asks, "What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?" (Luke 9:25). You could own everything and still lose the one thing that's you. I think that's a question worth sitting with.

The answer is when He comes in His glory. Jesus says, "If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory…" (Luke 9:26). This is one of the verses that keeps my ovens warm. It tells us He is coming in glory, but it doesn't tell us when.

The answer is the Father and the holy angels. Jesus says He comes "…in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels." (Luke 9:26). That's three glories in one sentence. Quite a list, friends.

The answer is the kingdom of God. Jesus says, "…some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God." (Luke 9:27). He opens with "…I tell you truly…" so I'm listening hard. And He's talking about people standing right there with Him.
